strategyOwner: Vitaly Smilianets / GTMx outbound (Kaylee Long thread)
headline: Your Awery waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing cargo airlines, GSAs/GSSAs, handlers, charter brokers, private operators, and aviation services into the right Awery ERP / CargoBooking / switch offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Vitaly Smilianets.
productSummary: Awery Aviation Software (awery.aero; assets also on awery.com CDN) sells a cloud / hosted aviation ERP + CRM platform for cargo airlines, cargo GSAs/GSSAs, cargo handling agents, OBC/courier companies, commercial airlines, private operators, air charter brokers, and aviation services providers. Homepage: Advanced Aviation Software Platform. Core product Awery ERP covers sales, operations, finance, and HR in one integrated web-based system (cloud on AWS or customer-hosted). Companion products: CargoBooking (airline–forwarder marketplace for rates and bookings; Oriental Sky Aviation signed as first Chinese GSSA), eMagic (AI extraction from emails), and a Documents Library for controlled distribution. Public proof points: Air Cargo News (May 2025) — more than 100 customers including about 45 GSAs; Wings on Board case — 25% productivity increase after Awery; Growjo/older copy — software solutions to 64 aviation businesses (superseded by 100+); Tracxn — ~69 employees as of Apr 2026; 2026 ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 surveillance audit with zero nonconformities; IATA partner / ONE Record contributor. Testimonials on-site: MixJet, Independent Aviation, Chapman Freeborn, Global Cargo Management, RUS Aviation. Kaylee's outbound thread already named three angles: (1) high-intent aviation/logistics leads to CFOs and Operations Managers at mid-sized companies, (2) compliance and workflow inefficiencies, (3) A/B scalability vs connectivity messaging.
coreInsight: Vitaly sells one integrated aviation ERP, not eight vertical products. Cargo airline vs GSA vs charter broker is a merge tag after routing, not a second waterfall. The single routing signal is ops_stack_state from industry directories + site scrape: a named competitor aviation ERP / cargo CMS already on the stack, a live digital booking or quote portal without a named ERP, a multi-station / multi-carrier footprint without either of those, or none of those. That ladder maps to Awery's live positioning (replace fragmented tools, CargoBooking connectivity, multi-company / multi-currency ERP) and to Kaylee's compliance / workflow / connectivity angles.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how the operator already runs aviation ops software
sections.takeaway: A directory + site scrape already names a competitor ERP/CMS, shows a live booking/quote portal, marks multi-station / multi-carrier scale, or none of those. That ops_stack_state is stronger than a title guess and cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM aviation operator
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Named competitor stack first, then digital portal without a named ERP, then multi-entity / multi-station scale, then every remaining in-TAM aviation company.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each ops stack state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Competitor stacks get a Switch / Side-by-Side Brief. Portal operators get a Digital Ops Consolidation Brief. Multi-entity operators get a Multi-Entity ERP Brief. The rest get the Aviation Ops Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the stack, wire the portal, consolidate multi-entity, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always aviation operators Awery already sells into. Operator type (cargo airline, GSA, handler, charter, private) is a merge tag. A/Bs sit on exclusive routes (compliance vs connectivity from Kaylee's thread).

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the ops state already visible on the site
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor stack, the booking portal, or the multi-station footprint, poke the workflow / compliance / connectivity pain that state implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the competitor-stack route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay CHAMP, IBS iCargo, Softaire, Hits, Mercator, or a peer and still leak finance–ops integration or CargoBooking-style connectivity. Prove reply density, then roll portal operators, multi-entity, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Aviation industry directories (IATA agency / GSA lists, TIACA, ACI handlers, charter-broker directories, Cirium / ch-aviation style carrier lists) plus Apollo headcount filters are the commercial TAM Vitaly already sells into: cargo airlines, GSAs/GSSAs, handlers, OBC/courier, commercial airlines, private operators, charter brokers, and aviation services. Public global TAM account count is not published on awery.aero; treat size as estimated (see awery-magnet-flags.txt) and keep each launch tier ≥~1,500 contacts where possible — niche may force smaller first waves with longer read windows.

The same directory + site pull returns ops_stack_state: competitor ERP/CMS named in careers, integrations, or partner pages; public cargo booking / charter quote / customer portal; multi-station or multi-airline principal lists — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Awery positioning on awery.aero (integrated ERP replacing fragmented tools, CargoBooking connectivity, multi-company / multi-currency, A-to-Z ops+finance) plus Kaylee's thread angles: mid-sized CFO / Ops Manager buyers, compliance and workflow inefficiencies, scalability vs connectivity A/B.
Buyer title (CEO / CFO / COO / Head of Cargo / Operations Manager) and operator_type are scrape filters and merge tags, not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the account is routed.

sources.name: Aviation directories (IATA / TIACA / ACI / GSA & charter broker lists / ch-aviation-style carrier indexes)
sources.delivers: In-TAM aviation operators plus operator_type and scale proxies (stations, airline principals). The TAM spine.

sources.name: Company website / careers / integrations scrape
sources.delivers: Named competitor stack (CHAMP Cargospot, IBS iCargo, Softaire, Hits, Mercator, peers), digital booking/quote portals, and Awery already-customer suppress when visible.

sources.name: BuiltWith / tech-detect (where aviation SaaS shows)
sources.delivers: Thin secondary signal for known cargo CMS footprints. Prefer site-named stack over absence-of-tool guesses.

sources.name: Apollo (after qualification)
sources.delivers: Work emails for CFO / Ops / Cargo / CEO titles on already-routed accounts (mid-size 10–200 emp band from Kaylee's campaign).

sources.name: Optional Awery customer suppress
sources.delivers: Current-customer exclusion when the signal is visible (100+ customers per Air Cargo News). Treat as suppress, not a tier.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND competitor_stack detected (CHAMP Cargospot, IBS iCargo, Softaire, Hits, Mercator, or peer named on site/careers/integrations) AND not already_customer
routingRules.why: They already pay a competing aviation ERP or cargo CMS. Strongest intent for an Awery switch using integrated ops+finance and published customer proof (100+ customers, Wings 25% productivity).

routingRules.if: in_tam AND has_booking_portal = true (cargo booking, charter quote, or customer track portal) AND no Tier-1 competitor_stack
routingRules.why: They already sell digitally but the back-office ERP is unspecified. Maps to Awery ERP + CargoBooking connectivity and Kaylee's connectivity angle.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND multi_entity_signal = true (multi-station, multi-airline GSA principals, multi-company footprint) AND no Tier 1-2 match
routingRules.why: Scale without a locked competitor stack. Awery's multi-company / multi-currency ERP and ~45 GSA customers are the proof path.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (aviation operators Awery lists on awery.aero). Softest CTA around workflow, compliance, and one-platform ops+finance. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Competitor aviation ERP / cargo CMS named
tiers.trigger: Site, careers, or integrations name CHAMP Cargospot, IBS iCargo, Softaire, Hits, Mercator, or another competitor aviation ERP/CMS; not already an Awery customer
tiers.pain: They already pay for a competing stack and still feel ops–finance fragmentation, slow quote-to-AWB cycles, or missing marketplace connectivity versus what modern GSAs and cargo airlines expect.
tiers.valueProp: Awery ERP: one integrated web platform for sales, ops, finance, and HR; CargoBooking connectivity; switch brief anchored to 100+ customers and Wings on Board's 25% productivity lift — not a lecture about what an aviation ERP is.
tiers.dataSource: Operator site + careers/integrations scrape for competitor names
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - they already buy this category
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; not published on awery.aero — keep each tier ≥~1,500 contacts before launch when the niche allows

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Live digital booking / quote portal, no named competitor ERP
tiers.trigger: Site advertises cargo booking, rate request, charter quote, or customer track portal without a Tier-1 named competitor stack
tiers.pain: Front-door digital selling is live but the back office is still email, spreadsheets, or a thin tool — so compliance, billing, and ops visibility lag the portal promise.
tiers.valueProp: Digital Ops Consolidation Brief: Awery ERP behind the portal plus CargoBooking for airline–forwarder connectivity. Matches Kaylee's connectivity / workflow angle.
tiers.dataSource: Site scrape for booking/quote/portal URLs and forms
tiers.replyDensity: High - visible digital intent, stack not locked

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Multi-station / multi-carrier / multi-entity footprint
tiers.trigger: In-TAM operator shows multi-station, multi-airline GSA principals, or multi-company footprint; no Tier 1-2 ops_stack_state
tiers.pain: Scale across stations or airline principals without one system of record means duplicated rates, CASS/billing pain, and weak management visibility.
tiers.valueProp: Multi-Entity ERP Brief: Awery multi-company / multi-currency ERP with GSA-proven footprint (~45 GSA customers per Air Cargo News).
tiers.dataSource: Directories + locations / principals pages on operator sites
tiers.replyDensity: Medium - clear scale pain, longer sales cycle

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM aviation operators
tiers.trigger: In-TAM aviation operator (cargo airline, GSA, handler, charter, private, OBC, aviation services) with a CFO / Ops / CEO decision maker and no Tier 1-3 ops_stack_state
tiers.pain: Day-to-day aviation workflows still depend on fragmented tools, so compliance, quote speed, and finance visibility leave money on the table.
tiers.valueProp: Soft Aviation Ops Playbook: one-platform ops+finance story, ISO-backed security posture, and Kaylee's compliance vs scalability framing. Soft CTA.
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM
